text:
The subject, Bilal Latif, a low‑risk freelance software developer, received a series of high‑value inbound IBFT transfers from a large number of distinct counterparties over a short 14‑day period. Between 1 May and 9 May 2026 he received ten inbound payments totalling PKR 735,000, with individual amounts ranging from PKR 22,000 to PKR 88,000 and originating from at least eight different individuals (Saad Zafar, Fahad Shafiq, Nimra Riaz, Waqas Naveed, Shahid Javed, Junaid Akhtar, Ayesha Latif and others). The typology engine flagged this pattern (many distinct inbound counterparties and a large share of inbound value leaving quickly) with a score of 360, exceeding the alert threshold of 300.

Within hours of the last inbound receipt, the account made two large outbound transfers: a PKR 147,000 wallet‑to‑wallet transfer to QuickPay wallet ***0932 on 9 May and a PKR 43,000 wallet transfer to the same wallet on 11 May, plus a PKR 135,000 cash withdrawal from an ATM on 11 May. The rapid movement of funds from numerous sources into the account and their swift exit to a digital wallet and cash is characteristic of a “mule” operation used to layer and integrate illicit proceeds. No adverse media, sanctions or PEP matches were found, and the customer was not contacted about the hold on the wallet transfers, further heightening concern. Accordingly, the activity warrants filing a Suspicious Transaction Report.
